**Operator-profile isolation.** `~/.claude/settings.json` SHA-256 before the pass:
`6B59D5547DB81E9F9977AFC6CC5FAEF376F769591CA2F50F841D577530DD0C99`. After: recorded at the foot of
this file. `~/.claude/plugins/data` was enumerated before the first hook run and was **empty** — no
`lw-watchtower*` directory exists on this machine at all, which is itself the fixture for the
state-resolution claims at `architecture.md:594-641`.

## Method

Claims were driven, not read. Every hook was invoked the way the CLI invokes it — a real child
`powershell` 5.1 process with the JSON payload arriving on a real byte pipe — against a throwaway
plugin root and a throwaway `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA`, per the harness shape in `tests/gate_delegate.ps1`
and `tests/state_resolution.ps1`. Structural claims (registration counts, matchers, timeouts,
default switch states) were counted out of the file the claim is about. Performance tables and dated
history are marked *unobservable from here* and were not re-measured; they are counted as tried.

Result classes: **reproduced** · **false** · **unobservable from here** · **true, undocumented
condition**.

`Session modes` (:523, three rungs observed — `observe-only`, `unverified`, `degraded`), `git_hygiene`
(:780), `self_health` (:858), `context_injection` (:883) and `failure_capture and healing` (:1017).

Every discrepancy found is on `docs/architecture.md`, and in two of the four cases
(`send_liveness_gate`'s abstain, the `HH` peak) `modules.md` or the source comments state the same
mechanism **correctly** — the architecture page is the one that drifted.

## Verdict

**Ship it. The one sentence to fix first is #262 — but it does not gate the release.**

The machinery is in better shape than the prose. Every mechanism I drove behaved exactly as
specified: all thirteen hook registrations, the five-event supervisor exit-2 table, the `alerted.json`
dedupe, the whole five-step state-resolution ladder including the file-mtime discriminator that the
page makes a point of, all three gates' default-off state and their deny/abstain paths, both
directions of the `log_rotation`/`failure_capture` independence, the 500-record carry-forward, the
signal bridge's absent-not-zero discipline across every discovered data directory, and the `HH` glyph
table's four states. 76 of 87 claims reproduced, and none of the eight `modules.md` sections I
drove was wrong about anything — though three of its eleven sections were not reached and are
unaudited. Two of the four false claims are on a page whose *sibling* page states the same mechanism
correctly — this is documentation drift on one file, not a product that does not work.

**The single worst thing I saw** is [#262](https://github.com/LEAPWare-Software/LEAPWare-Watchtower/issues/262):
`architecture.md` tells the reader that the `HH` indicator's fault count is a peak that "is lowered by
nothing", and it is not — it is the newest `Stop` gauge, so a session that recorded five failed
background tasks renders the **green all-clear** after a single clean turn end. The code is defensible
and its own comments explain the gauge reasoning; the page is what is wrong. It matters more than a
docs bug normally would because of what this plugin claims to be: `architecture.md:727` says *"An
indicator that says healthy when it read nothing is worse than no indicator"*, `:836-838` records the
`GM` segment being deleted for going green with a trip still outstanding, and `:973` lists "rendered
unconditional green" as a shipped defect. A page that teaches an operator to read green as
"nothing has failed this session" reintroduces, in prose, the exact failure the rest of the document
is a monument to catching.

**The counter-argument, stated because it bears on severity.** The glyph table at `arch:719-720` —
which is what an operator actually reads to interpret the row — says green means *"the logs were read
and this session is clean"* and red means *"n **outstanding** faults"*. That is gauge language, and it
matches the code. So the page is right in two places and wrong in one, and a reader who never opens
the "Health and healing" section is not misled. I filed #262 as `sev:high` on the brief's test — a
claim that is false in a way that changes what a reader does — because *"lowered by nothing"* tells an
operator a red `HH` cannot clear itself, which is the opposite of what it does. An owner who weighs
the glyph table as the primary surface could reasonably carry it at `sev:medium`; that judgement is
recorded on the issue rather than settled here.
